front: Unlike in the physical sciences, conducting research in the field of Sociology is problematic.
back: Conducting sociological research is problematic in ways physical science research is not, since human subjects are self-aware, reactive, and value-laden, unlike inert natural phenomena.

front: None of the sociological perspectives is fully independent of the others
back: Sociological perspectives overlap and inform one another; no single perspective operates in complete isolation from the others, so the statement is true.

front: The study of the underlying rules of behaviour that guide group interaction is ……
back: Ethnomethodology is defined as the study of the methods/underlying rules people use to make sense of and guide their everyday group interactions.

front: The branch of sociology concerned with the analysis of elementary forms and processes of social behaviour at the interpe...
back: Micro-sociology is concerned with the analysis of elementary forms and processes of social behaviour that occur relatively informally at the interpersonal level in face-to-face contexts and small groups.

front: Sociology as a whole, concerned with broad-scale or grand-scale analysis of complex organizations such as bureaucracies...
back: Macro-sociology, also known as systematic sociology, studies society as a whole, concerned with broad-scale analysis of complex organizations, institutions, and social change.

front: Which theories are most often associated with the microscopic level of sociological analysis?
back: Exchange Theory, Symbolic Interaction theory, Phenomenology-Ethnomethodology, and Action Theory are the theories most commonly associated with the microscopic level of sociological analysis, focused on individual action and interaction.

front: According to the course material, which two research methods are most often applied at the microscopic level of sociolog...
back: The experiment and participant observation are the two methods most often applied at the microscopic level of sociological analysis, since both focus closely on individual behaviour and interaction.

front: According to Bogdan and Taylor (1975), methodology in the social sciences refers broadly to:
back: Bogdan and Taylor (1975) define methodology, in the broad sense, as the process, principles, and procedures by which researchers approach problems and seek answers — closely tied to underlying assumptions, interests, and goals.
